notes: The whole book read as one pass, digitized text from the Internet Archive (historyofcityofs00hitt; loc.gov's own item page returns a Cloudflare challenge to automated fetches). Programmatic scan for numbered-address mentions across all ~245 sections, followed by full manual reading of the two sections that carry building-level detail (§29/32 Village Era, §231 Sources of Buildings, §237 Hotels) plus §238 Millionaires and §239 Extravagance, which named no addresses at all. This closes out the book: every numbered address anywhere in the text is accounted for, either already known from the first 2026-08-04 pass or newly found and resolved/declined here.

coverage.remaining: None. The whole book (20,323 OCR lines) has now been read for address-level facts; hittell-1878 moves from open to done.
coverage.note: 20 candidate building-level facts found: 5 numbered addresses (all already known from the first pass — 2 already published, 3 with no EAS record), 8 dated-or-named hotels resolvable only to a corner, 1 site-history fact resolved to an existing page but declined for lacking a date, and 17 further corner-only funding anecdotes in §231 folded into one entry. Zero of the newly-examined material yielded a new page or a new fact fit to publish; the two already-published facts (400 and 420 Montgomery) were already on their pages from the first pass and are recorded here for the first time.

findings.address_as_written: on the site of the present bank of California
findings.description: The Tehama House, a two-story frame hotel patronized by army officers, stood on the site later occupied by the Bank of California's building.

citation.label: John S. Hittell, A History of the City of San Francisco and Incidentally of the State of California (San Francisco: A. L. Bancroft & Company, 1878), section 237

raw.text: The Tehama house, a two-story frame on the site of the present bank of California, had the patronage of the army officers

resolution.method: SF Planning's historic-resource-by-parcel dataset names APN 0239003 “BANK OF CALIFORNIA”, matching Hittell's “present bank of California”; the existing page already carries the Bank of California building history.

publish.note: Hittell gives no year for the Tehama House itself (it is placed only relative to the 1847 City Hotel and 1849 St. Francis, before the post-1860 hotel wave); the evidence bar needs a date and this passage doesn't supply one. Leaving unpublished rather than guessing a decade.

findings.address_as_written: corner locations named in §231, ‘Sources of Buildings’, with no street number
findings.description: Seventeen further buildings named only by corner and funding anecdote, with no street number, year or lot dimension: the Palace Hotel (William Sharon, via Crown Point and Belcher bonanza profits), the Nevada Block (Consolidated Virginia bullion), two buildings on the eastern corners of Pine and Montgomery (Gould and Curry / Savage bonanza), the Cosmopolitan Hotel (three brothers from the Sierra Buttes gold quartz mine), Watts's building (south-east corner of Clay and Kearny, Eureka mine at Grass Valley), a wooden building on the north-west corner of Stockton and O'Farrell (Plato mine), the Occidental Hotel's foundation (the city's first foundry), the Nucleus Building (east corner of Market and Third), Montgomery Block (Halleck, Peachy & Billings), the Russ House (a soldier's 1847 land-commission lots), the Lick House (an early town-lot investment), Friedlander's building (north-east corner of California and Sansome, wheat speculation), the Odd Fellows' Hall (north-west corner of Montgomery and Sutter, built by J. W. Tucker), a house on the north-east corner of California and Leidesdorff (Pacific Insurance Company, bankrupted by the 1871 Chicago fire), Stephen A. Wright's building (north-west corner of Montgomery and Jackson, built with depositors' money before the panic of February 1855), and the buildings of the San Francisco Stock Exchange and the Pacific Exchange.

citation.label: John S. Hittell, A History of the City of San Francisco and Incidentally of the State of California (San Francisco: A. L. Bancroft & Company, 1878), section 231

raw.text: Common rumor tells us of the sources of the money invested in many of the prominent buildings of San Francisco. The Crown Point and Belcher bonanza furnished Mr. Sharon with the means for becoming the owner of the Palace hotel...

resolution.method: None of these seventeen carry a street number, and Hittell gives no lot dimensions for any of them, so corner.py has nothing to test a candidate parcel against. SF Planning's historic-resource name index was queried for each building name (City Hotel, St. Francis, Oriental, Tehama, Russ House, Lick House, Occidental Hotel, Grand Hotel, Montgomery Block, Cosmopolitan Hotel, Odd Fellows, Nevada Block, Palace Hotel financing) and returned no match beyond the Palace Hotel's existing 1875-opening entry, which the page already carries from a stronger source.
resolution.note: One consolidated entry for seventeen otherwise-unresolvable corner anecdotes in the same section, rather than seventeen near-identical rejected entries; kept together so a future run doesn't re-read this passage.

publish.note: No street number on any of the seventeen; cannot resolve without guessing.
